# Draft:Empire East Land Holdings

----
Empire East Land Holdings, Inc. ([https://www.pse.com.ph/company-information-ELI/ PSE:ELI]), also known as Empire East, is a real estate company located in the Philippines. It is a subsidiary of Megaworld Corporation. Previously, it was known as Megaworld's Community Housing Division, before it was spun off and incorporated on July 15, 1994.
Developments
Empire East's developments are centered on the middle-income sector. It has built projects across cities in Metro Manila and CALABARZON.
In Metro Manila:
* Little Baguio Gardens
* Governor's Place
* Kingswood Makati
* Gilmore Heights
* San Francisco Gardens
* Greenhills Garden Square
* Xavier Hills
* California Garden Square
* Cambridge Village
* San Lorenzo Place
* Pioneer Woodlands
* The Rochester
* Kasara Urban Resort Residences
* Little Baguio Terraces
* Covent Garden
* Mango Tree Residences
In CALABARZON:
* Laguna BelAir
* The Sonoma
Upcoming Projects:
* The Paddington Place
* Empire East Highland City
Controversies
Service Issues
Pioneer Woodlands was featured on ABS-CBN's TV Patrol segment called, calling out the developer for issues surrounding its then pre-selling units.
A Facebook group named "Megaworld Pissed Buyers," comprising hundreds of property owners, has created a petition on Change.org urging Megaworld and Empire East founder Andrew Tan to address numerous issues. These concerns include unfair payment terms, significant delays in the turnover of units, deficiencies in documentation and financing, as well as construction defects, leading to regret among the buyers regarding their purchases concerning their property .
Legal Dispute with MPower
California Garden Square, one of the properties developed by Empire East, was involved in a legal dispute with the Meralco subsidiary MPower, which claims that the project has outstanding obligations amounting to P42 million. Kevin Tan, the CEO of Megaworld, refuted claims that the real estate developer owed funds to MPower. He clarified that although Empire East is responsible for the development of California Garden Square, the property has long been under the ownership and management of the California Garden Square Condominium Association (CSGSCAI).
